summary: Cluster A closed. login.code.sub no longer contradicts the SMS in the guest's hand: the TTL is interpolated as {{minutes}} from auth-ttl.ts — the client's single copy of the API's CODE_TTL_MINUTES (5), defined once, because no response DTO carries the value (OtpRequestedDto/MagicLinkRequestedDto are {ok} only). login.magicLink.sub (15) gets the identical treatment. The drift guard is NOT a tautology: e2e/login-ttl.spec.ts parses the API's own constants off the sibling wedding-api checkout and compares them to the imported client constants — two numbers in two repos, either can move alone — skipping VISIBLY if the sibling is absent (the suite is local-only per rule 11, so it is present wherever the suite runs). Bite proven: client constant set back to 10 → 'wedding-api's CODE_TTL_MINUTES and the client's copy disagree'. The month sweep then found the same defect wearing dates: schedule.header spelled 'SAT · 5 JUN' ×3, the schedule template hardcoded 'SAT · 5 JUN 2027' untranslated in HTML, and yesTitle spelled 'See you in June' — all now derived from the configured date via new helpers (T393's conventions); dashboard.plan.caption drops its transcribed 'next 3'; four dead DS-mock keys hardcoding date/city deleted (845→840 keys/locale, sets identical). GUARD B ships: no month name anywhere in any locale file, empty allowlist. Nothing in cluster B was touched: T397 (run first) had already closed the absolutes the sweep crossed. Unit 663→672; e2e 485/455→505/475 passed, 0 failed; transfer 195.77 kB unchanged.

acceptance.criterion: login.code.sub states the real TTL, and takes it from a single source rather than a second literal. If the value cannot reach the client today, interpolate a constant defined once and say in the report where the client's copy of it lives and what keeps it honest.
acceptance.evidence: The value cannot reach the client today: the generated client's OtpRequestedDto and MagicLinkRequestedDto carry only {ok: boolean} — no response in the OTP flow exposes the TTL. The client's copy therefore lives in src/app/core/helper/auth-ttl.ts (OTP_CODE_TTL_MINUTES = 5, MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MINUTES = 15), the only place either numeral exists client-side; login.ts exposes them and login.html passes minutes into both auth-heading subParams; all six locale strings say '{{minutes}} minutes/minutos' with no literal. What keeps it honest: e2e/login-ttl.spec.ts imports the client constants and parses the API's (wedding-api sms-verification.service.ts CODE_TTL_MINUTES; magic-link.service.ts TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES) off the sibling checkout, asserting equality — the exact pattern the SMS template already uses server-side ({{TTL_MINUTES}} interpolated from the constant), applied across the repo boundary. A missing sibling checkout skips with a message that names itself as the whole point of the test, never a silent pass.

acceptance.criterion: Run the month-name/duration sweep across all three locales; fix what is in this cluster and report anything that belongs to cluster B without touching it — that is T397's.
acceptance.evidence: Swept all three locales for month names (accent-aware), '<n> <unit>' durations, and bare numerals, plus templates. FIXED, all cluster A: [1] login.code.sub + login.magicLink.sub (above). [2] schedule.header — 'SAT · 5 JUN'/'SÁB · 5 JUN'/'SAM · 5 JUI' — the wedding date, a config field, spelled ×3 (fr's 'JUI' was also ambiguous with juillet); now weddingDayLabel(config.date, lang) via a HeaderService effect, key deleted. [3] schedule.html hardcoded 'SAT · 5 JUN 2027' as untranslated template text — worse than a locale literal (violates rule 8 too); now bound to the same helper with year. [4] rsvp.create.confirm.yesTitle 'See you in June'/'Hasta junio'/'À bientôt en juin' → 'See you in {{month}}' via weddingMonthLabel(config.date); unit test proves a moved date renders its own month. [5] dashboard.plan.caption 'next 3 coming up' — 3 is dashboard.ts's slice(0,3), and the copy was false whenever fewer than 3 milestones remained; the numeral is dropped, no plumbing. [6] Four dead DS-mock keys hardcoding date/city, referenced nowhere (grepped src + e2e): invitee.countdown.date ('5 June 2027 · Granada'), invitee.busNote, invitee.busNoteDate, schedule.timeline — deleted ×3 locales rather than allowlisted as unused. CLUSTER B: nothing to hand over — T397 ran first in this session and the sweep crossed no absolute it had not already fixed. REPORTED, NOT TOUCHED (neither cluster, see risks/decisions): WEDDING_DATE hardcoded in wedding-date.ts duplicating config.date (code, not copy — drives the countdowns); travel.subtitle's '20 min to City Center' (authored prose, the number is nobody's constant); shared.nickname.hint 'Max 30 characters' (the clamp is client code and unit-tested at 30).

acceptance.criterion: A drift guard, per T391's method. For the TTL specifically: a test that fails if the rendered string and the API's value disagree. If the client cannot see the API value, say so plainly — an honest 'this cannot be checked from here' is worth more than a test that re-asserts the literal it is supposed to be guarding.
acceptance.evidence: The client cannot see the API value at runtime — said plainly above and in both files' headers. But 'from here' is a local e2e suite in a documented four-repo checkout, and from HERE the API's source is readable: login-ttl.spec.ts is a genuine cross-repo comparison, not the tautology the task warns about — no test re-asserts '5'; the client side is the imported constant, the API side is parsed from wedding-api's source, and the live half renders the code screen and asserts the constant's own value reaches it (no literal re-typed even there). Bite proven by reproducing the original defect: OTP_CODE_TTL_MINUTES set to 10 → the cross-repo test fails naming both files; reverted, green. The honest limit is stated in the spec header and risks[]: where the sibling checkout is absent the check skips visibly instead of lying either way. Plus T394's GUARD B for the date-shaped subset: rsvp-deadline.spec.ts now sweeps EVERY locale value for month names (en case-sensitive — 'May' month vs 'may' verb; es/fr insensitive), allowlist empty today, so the next transcribed date fails the suite at authoring time.

risks.risk: The cross-repo TTL check is only as good as the four-repo layout: where ../wedding-api is not checked out, it skips. The skip is loud and self-describing, but a permanently-skipped check is no check — if the e2e suite ever moves to CI without the sibling repo, the TTL pair is unguarded again.
risks.surfaces_at: The day a .github workflow runs pnpm test:e2e (CLAUDE.md rule 11 notes none does today); that change should either check out wedding-api alongside or replace the file-parse with an exposed-TTL API field.

risks.risk: The schedule header and date badge are now empty until the wedding config lands (they were instant, from the locale file). On a slow connection that is a briefly blank header instead of a wrong date — the trade T393 already made for the deadline, made here for the date. The fr badge also changed 'JUI' → 'JUIN' (the old abbreviation collided with juillet).
risks.surfaces_at: Visual review of the schedule screen on a throttled connection; the DS parity specs passed unchanged.

risks.risk: WEDDING_DATE in wedding-date.ts (new Date(2027, 5, 5), venue in the comment) is the config's `date` transcribed into CODE — it drives daysUntilWedding for the dashboard and guest countdowns. Same mechanism as this cluster, but in a .ts file where no locale sweep sees it; if the couple moves the date in Settings, every countdown is silently wrong.
risks.surfaces_at: Any change to the configured wedding date; the decision below proposes the fix.

risks.risk: Two transcribed numerals were left by judgement, reported not fixed: travel.subtitle's '20 min to City Center' (authored prose — no system constant owns it, so there is nothing to interpolate from) and shared.nickname.hint's 'Max 30 characters' (the clamp is client code, unit-tested at 30, but the hint and the clamp can still drift).
risks.surfaces_at: travel copy edits (the couple's wording to change, ADR-0046 territory); any change to the nickname clamp — worth a shared constant if it ever moves.

decisions_needed.question: WEDDING_DATE is hardcoded in src/app/core/helper/wedding-date.ts while the API serves the same value as config `date` — the countdowns (dashboard.service, guest.service, home-today) all run off the constant. Derive them from configuration, or keep the constant?
options: Derive daysUntilWedding from ConfigurationService.weddingConfigPublic()?.date (a small task: the helpers become date-taking functions, the services compute from the config signal, undefined-before-load renders the countdown blank briefly) — removes the last transcription of the date and makes a moved wedding correct everywhere at once.

Keep the constant and accept the transcription (it predates this phase, the wedding date is the least likely config value to move, and the blank-until-loaded trade would now touch the public invitation's countdown) — documented here so the next reader knows it is a decision, not an oversight.
decisions_needed.recommendation: Option 1, filed as its own small task — this session did not take it because it touches the public invitation surface beyond T396's locale-file scope, and the countdown-blank trade deserves its own acceptance criteria. Until then the constant is at least named, documented and single.
decisions_needed.needed_by: Before any real change to the configured wedding date; practically, the next grooming of phase 33.
